spans.claim: Dr. Weathered was found dead in the Domino Club wearing an Inquisitor costume
spans.anchor: Within the curtains, stretched at full length on a low divan, was a figure attired as an Inquisitor
spans.span: Within the curtains, stretched at full length on a low divan, was a figure attired as an Inquisitor.

spans.claim: The victim carried opium pellets in his waistcoat pocket
spans.anchor: he extracted a silver matchbox from the waistcoat, and opened it... two pellets the size of small peas

spans.claim: The safe at Dr. Weathered’s house was found open with keys left inside
spans.anchor: The door of the safe standing wide open. The key was in the keyhole, with the whole bunch, including the latchkey, dangling from it
spans.span: There the first sight that met their eyes was the door of the safe standing wide open. The key was in the keyhole, with the whole bunch, including the latchkey, dangling from it.

spans.claim: Lady Violet Bredwardine’s name appeared in the club’s members list and appointment book
spans.anchor: Lady Violet Bredwardine... was also one of Weathered’s patients, which means that she may have been in his power

spans.claim: Lady Violet had a solid alibi being at Tyberton Castle during the murder
spans.anchor: Lady Violet Bredwardine is down in Herefordshire at her father’s seat, Tyberton Castle. She left London for the Castle the day before yesterday
spans.span: You can tell Sir Frank that Lady Violet Bredwardine is down in Herefordshire at her father's seat, Tyberton Castle. She left London for the Castle the day before yesterday by the noon train, so that she can't have been present at the Domino Club.

spans.claim: The rare poison upasine was identified as the cause of death
spans.anchor: There is one drug known to me which does in fact produce appearances exactly like those we have seen... I have called it upasine

spans.claim: Madame Bonnell was the proprietor of the Domino Club and had access to the victim
spans.anchor: Madame Bonnell, the proprietress of the club... She had obviously employed her time since the discovery of this particular mischance in making the best of her personal appearance

spans.claim: Madame Bonnell’s bottle contained harmless powder, not the real poison
spans.anchor: The powder now in this bottle is a harmless mixture of charcoal and common salt
spans.span: The powder now in this bottle is a harmless mixture of charcoal and common salt.

spans.claim: Madame Bonnell’s fingerprint matched a wanted criminal in France
spans.anchor: You have dyed your hair, Leonie Marchand, since I saw you last, but you haven’t changed your finger-print
spans.span: You have dyed your hair, Leonie Marchand, since I saw you last, but you haven't changed your finger-print, you know.

spans.claim: The poison bottle was stolen from Mrs. Amelia Baker’s house
spans.anchor: The bottle is gone!... The bottle of upasine was not there

spans.claim: Mrs. Neobard secretly took the poison bottle from her husband’s house
spans.anchor: I took a bunch of all the keys I could find in the house... almost the first key I tried opened the chiffonier and there stood the bottle

spans.claim: The blackmail advertisement was placed by a solicitor with false names
spans.anchor: The names in the advertisement are bogus ones... The man’s real name is Stillman

spans.claim: Dr. Cassilis disguised himself as Zenobia to meet Dr. Weathered
spans.anchor: I had to disguise myself in a costume with which he was familiar... the Zenobia helmet

spans.claim: Sarah Neobard accused Lady Violet of poisoning Dr. Weathered
spans.anchor: I saw her drop something into his cup
spans.span: _I saw her drop something into his cup.

spans.claim: Lady Violet lent her costume to Dr. Cassilis
spans.anchor: She lent me the Zenobia costume

spans.claim: Dr. Weathered was a blackmailer who kept secret letters from patients
spans.anchor: The doctor’s case-book that was missing, the book containing the secrets of the women
spans.span: It was the doctor's case-book that was missing, the book containing the secrets of the women.

spans.claim: The rare poison upasine causes skin to look like parchment
spans.anchor: the whole surface of the skin was corrugated by tiny wrinkles, so that it presented the appearance of a mummy dried by the embalmer
spans.span: The grayness I had remarked had grown deeper, and the whole surface of the skin was corrugated by tiny wrinkles, so that it presented the appearance of a mummy dried by the embalmer.

spans.claim: Madame Bonnell bribed the waiter Gerard to watch Dr. Weathered’s drinks
spans.anchor: your continued hints made Gerard watchful, and on the fatal night he did see something dropped in the doctor’s cup
spans.span: What really happened was that your continued hints made Gerard watchful, and on the fatal night he did see something dropped in the doctor's cup by a dancer whom he described correctly.

spans.claim: The murder was motivated by Madame Bonnell’s desire to protect her position and extort money
spans.anchor: She was ready to help me on her own terms. I undertook to transfer the whole property in the Domino Club to her on my husband’s death
